_comment: [OPUS-4.8] sq-c5f gate-count regression baseline. Checked-in ultra_honk `circuit_size` (bb gates, the noir-optimisation ground truth) per compiled zk/compose member. The `gate_count_regression` test (tests/gate_count.rs) recompiles each member, reads its real circuit_size, and FAILS if it exceeds baseline*(1+tolerance) — preventing silent circuit bloat. Tolerance is 3% (see the test): bb gate counts for the scan members vary ~0.5-0.75% across platform/build (measured: darwin arm64 baseline vs linux x86_64 +0.75% on scan_k2_n64_r8; filter members are byte-identical), so 3% absorbs platform noise while still catching real relation growth (typically tens of %). To re-baseline after an INTENTIONAL circuit change, run `bench/zk-compose/scripts/gate_counts.sh` and copy the new circuit_size values here (and into bench/zk-compose/gate_counts_latest.json).

_comment_g5: [OPUS-4.8] sq-ncvq.8 (Gate G5): `snapshot_covers_every_member` enforces a baseline for every `zk/compose/` proving member; `snapshot_covers_top_level_circuits` (tests/gate_count.rs) extends that coverage to EVERY `bin`-type Noir package elsewhere under `zk/` — a new top-level circuit family. Such a circuit must have either a `members` baseline row OR an `exempt_circuits` entry (with a reason), so a deployable circuit cannot ship without a gate-count baseline. Non-deployed `bin` packages (e.g. test harnesses) belong in `exempt_circuits`. [OPUS-4.8] sq-5reoy: the zk/ieee754 and zk/xpath trees were externalized to the sparq-org/noir_IEEE754 and sparq-org/noir_XPath face repos (#1599), so zk/compose is now the only proving-circuit family in-tree and there are no top-level `bin` packages outside it — `exempt_circuits` is intentionally empty (the former xpath_unit_tests harness lives in the face repo's CI now).
_comment_sq_dgb9q: [OPUS-4.8] sq-dgb9q (#1060, flow-on from #1006): there is NO monolithic top-level `zk/compose` proving circuit to baseline. `zk/compose` is a `[workspace]` ROOT (no `[package]`, no `main.nr`, no `circuit_size`); composition is verified HOST-SIDE by the Rust `verify_manifest` path over per-member proofs (crates/sparq-zk-compose/src/verifier.rs), NOT by one aggregating Noir circuit. So coverage is COMPLETE without a separate top-level row: every deployable proving circuit is a compose `bin` member with a `members` baseline, guarded by `snapshot_covers_every_member` (family members) + `snapshot_covers_top_level_circuits` (any `bin` elsewhere under `zk/`, Gate G5). A top-level compose row is not added because no such circuit exists — and a gate number is never fabricated for a non-existent circuit.

_comment_sq_l15mi: [SONNET-4.6] sq-7pifo re-baseline: hidden_issuer_d4 16946 -> 24452 (+44.29%). This is the INTENTIONAL, correctness-motivated cost of the sq-l15mi torsion-key soundness fix (#1962), which added the prime-order-subgroup guards `assert_in_prime_order_subgroup(pk)` and `...(r)` to `compose_core::issuer::schnorr_verify` — two extra 251-bit `scalar_mul(BJJ_L, .)` decompositions on the hidden-issuer path, closing a no-secret Schnorr forgery via a cofactor-8 torsion key. It was never re-baselined because `gate_count_regression` ran in NO CI lane; sq-7pifo's new zk-toolchain step is what finally surfaced it. ATTRIBUTION IS EXACT, not assumed: recompiling zk/compose at 2b5d0739^ (the commit before the fix) with the pinned toolchain measures hidden_issuer_d4 at exactly 16946, and every OTHER member measured byte-identical to its baseline — so the whole +7506 delta is that one fix, not accumulated drift. Not a soundness claim: the composition verifier remains NOT-yet-sound pending external audit (sq-qhy4).

_comment_sq_wz99x: [OPUS-5] sq-wz99x (research/zk-field-native-encoding.md sec 13.5): the filter_value_dl_datetime member (the xsd:dateTime / xsd:date value lane; ONE member for BOTH lanes -- the lane lives in the public datatype_const). Baseline 3070 = filter_value_dl_decimal's. PROVENANCE, STATED EXACTLY -- this number was NOT produced by running `bb gates` on this box: bb 5.0.0-nightly.20260324 was not obtainable here (the pinned release URL 404s), so only the nargo half of the pinned toolchain was run. What WAS measured, with the PINNED nargo 1.0.0-beta.21: `nargo compile --workspace` emits target/filter_value_dl_datetime.json whose `bytecode` field is BYTE-IDENTICAL to target/filter_value_dl_decimal.json's (sha256 320841ba616afd0a330e5d21103318b9efc02ed35823480e4a989cc7555c2bd4, 1836 bytes, both) -- the two members compile to the SAME ACIR, because the relation IS the decimal relation with a renamed public input (only the ABI parameter NAME bound_scaled -> bound_scaled_epoch differs; the ABI types + visibilities are identical). `bb gates -s ultra_honk` is a deterministic function of that bytecode, so the circuit_size is necessarily the decimal member's 3070, not an estimate. The zk-toolchain lane's `gate_count_regression` runs the real `bb gates` and will fail loudly if that reasoning is ever wrong. To re-verify the ACIR identity without bb: run `nargo compile --workspace` in zk/compose and compare the two `bytecode` fields. NOT a soundness change: the verifier remains NOT-yet-sound pending external audit (sq-qhy4), and the sec 13 rule set is itself an open audit obligation (CR-G8).

_comment_filter_value_dl_bool: The filter_value_dl_bool member: the DUAL-LEAF BIT-DOMAIN xsd:boolean value lane (the dedicated boolean sibling of filter_value_dl_int, with the same public layout plus the {0, 1} constraints on the witnessed handle and the public bound). Baseline 3032 MEASURED on linux x86_64 with the PINNED toolchain (nargo 1.0.0-beta.21 / bb 5.0.0-nightly.20260324) by `bb gates -s ultra_honk` on target/filter_value_dl_bool.json. ATTRIBUTION, checked rather than assumed: compiling zk/compose from a clean archive of the pre-change commit and from this tree produced BYTE-IDENTICAL ACIR bytecode for all 69 pre-existing members (sha256 over each target/<member>.json `bytecode` field), so no other baseline here moves and the new row is the only addition. Structurally the member differs from filter_value_dl_int in exactly one place: where that member range-decomposes the value handle into u64 (assert_max_bit_size::<64>()), this one constrains the handle and the bound with v*(v-1)==0. The measured size lands one gate below filter_value_dl_int's 3033; no apportioning of that single gate between the two constructions is claimed. NOT a soundness change: the verifier remains NOT-yet-sound pending external audit (sq-qhy4), and the value lane keeps the documented INV-VL downgrade (CR-G8).
